report.summary: Chunk 7 of 9: implements _estimated_tokens fallback, build_context_plan, and DSSReceipt dataclass with to_dict, content_sha256, envelope.
risks: build_context_plan | medium | Greedy packing may omit high-score items due to order; sorting by (-score, node_id) is deterministic but not optimal. | Clarify if optimality is required or if greedy is acceptable.

handoff.purpose: Implement token estimation fallback, context plan building, and DSS receipt dataclass.

symbols.name: _estimated_tokens
symbols.note: Returns estimated tokens for a node. Falls back to loc*8 if no measured cost. (Line 721-736)

symbols.name: build_context_plan
symbols.note: Greedily packs file nodes into token budget. Raises KeyError for unknown or non-file node IDs. (Line 738-790)

symbols.name: DSSReceipt
symbols.note: Dataclass for content-addressed provenance. Includes to_dict, content_sha256, envelope. (Line 792-830)

symbols.name: DSSReceipt.to_dict
symbols.note: Returns dict of receipt fields with sorted input_sha256 and relation_channels. (Line 799-808)

symbols.name: DSSReceipt.envelope
symbols.note: Returns dict with receipt_sha256 plus to_dict(). (Line 813-816)

claims.text: A deterministic documented fallback; callers should pass measured costs when context budgeting must correspond to a specific tokenizer.
claims.why: The fallback loc*8 is deterministic and the docstring explains it's a fallback.

claims.text: It is also the reason ``build_context_plan`` refuses non-file node kinds BEFORE calling this: this fallback cannot fail, so for a node with no bytes on disk it does not report a gap, it reports 8 tokens. The guard upstream is what keeps that number honest -- do not relax it here.
claims.why: build_context_plan (lines 762-770) raises KeyError for non-file node kinds before calling _estimated_tokens, consistent with the claim.

claims.text: "Whole-file" is enforced, not assumed. Membership in the forest is not enough to be packable: only ``FILE_NODE_KINDS`` name something with bytes on disk, and a plan is a list of things to READ. A ``type``/``field`` node is valid evidence and an invalid candidate, and the two failures are reported separately -- an unknown id is a typo, a known id of the wrong kind is a category error -- because collapsing them would send the author of either one looking for the other's bug.
claims.why: build_context_plan raises KeyError for unknown node_id (line 763) and for non-file node kinds (lines 764-769), reporting separate errors.

claims.text: Refusing loudly rather than skipping quietly is the same posture ``restrict_scores`` and ``semantic_super_sample`` already take on their own inputs.
claims.why: restrict_scores and semantic_super_sample are not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Nothing inside this module can trigger it: ``_relation_adjacencies`` keeps diffusion file-to-file, so a type node has no path into ``fused``. That makes this the SECOND lock on the door, and the one that turns a regression in the first into a stack trace instead of a fabricated cost.
claims.why: _relation_adjacencies and fused are not defined in this chunk.

observations.what: The fallback token estimation uses loc*8, where loc is max(1, node.attributes.get('loc',1)). This is deterministic but may not reflect actual token count.

build_context_plan sorts candidates by (-score, node_id) and then greedily packs. This may omit high-score items if they exceed remaining budget, while lower-score items that fit earlier may be included.
DSSReceipt.to_dict sorts input_sha256 and relation_channels by key, but not other dict fields. This ensures deterministic serialization for hashing.
DSSReceipt.envelope adds receipt_sha256 key with value of content_sha256, then spreads to_dict(). This embeds the hash inside the envelope.
